$comment: Config for scripts/check-pr-review-signal.mjs (issue #3312).
This file lives under scripts/, and .github/workflows/pr-review-signal.yml carries NO
path filter, so the job that reads it fires on every pull_request event regardless of
which files changed. That is deliberate: #3305's gate could not fire on the file it
guarded because that file was in no path filter, and a presence check that can itself be
filtered out is the same defect.
`reviewers` are the check CONTEXTS whose descriptions are adjudicated. Adding an
unrelated context here would make this gate opine on free text it has no business
reading; keep it to bot reviewers that claim a verdict on the code.
`phrases` are matched as case-insensitive PREFIXES of the description, and only against
a `success` state. `neutral` and `failure` already communicate 'no verdict'.
`excludeJobKeys` drops `test` -- the `Build + WASM + Rust + Node` aggregate. It is
`needs:` twelve jobs and publishes NO check run until every one of them finishes, so
waiting for it means waiting out the whole matrix. Measured by `created_at` -- when a
lane becomes PRESENT, which is what this gate polls for, not `started_at` -- from each
run's own creation, over the 68 completed test.yml PR runs of 2026-08-25/26 that
published it: the aggregate appeared at min 509, median 894, max 2067 seconds, with 33
of the 68 past the 900 s budget then in force. The last NON-aggregate lane appeared at min 161,
median 190, p95 522, max 845 seconds: 0 of the 68 past it. Requiring the aggregate makes
the wait a function of the SUITE's total runtime, which grows, and would false-fail half
of every green PR; requiring only the lanes makes it a function of how fast GitHub
creates check runs. Nothing is lost: the aggregate is one of only two contexts in main's ruleset, so
branch protection already blocks on it, and the #3294 total-absence shape still fails
here naming all fifteen lanes. Asserted in check-pr-review-signal.test.mjs.
`reviewVerdictSeverity` is `warn`, and that is a considered downgrade rather than a
retreat -- see the note on the key itself.

$reviewVerdictSeverityComment: WARN, NOT FAIL, AND THE EVIDENCE IS THAT A RATE-LIMITED STATUS NEVER SELF-HEALS.
The full status history on such a SHA is `queued -> in progress -> success/Review rate
limited`, and then nothing, forever. The quota recovers; the status on that commit does
not. So `fail` means red until a human pushes a commit or triggers an on-demand review --
on 8 of the 19 open PRs measured the day this shipped. That is exactly the class this repo
already ruled on when it marked check-coderabbit-review.mjs and check-pr-green.mjs
`@unwired-by-design`: 'a required check built on transient GitHub state fails for reasons
unrelated to the diff under test'. The finding is still printed and still quotes the
reviewer verbatim, so nothing is hidden -- it just does not hold the PR red on a quota.
The LANE half has no knob and cannot be downgraded: a missing test lane is a fact about
$reviewAuthorsComment: PART 3 (issue #3312, louistrue: 'A review whose commit_id is not the PR head has not
reviewed the PR'). `reviewAuthors` maps a REVIEW AUTHOR's GitHub login to the CHECK
CONTEXT that same reviewer publishes under. The two identity spaces are different --
the login is `coderabbitai[bot]`, the context is `CodeRabbit` -- and the default policy
needs both: it fires only when the CONTEXT claims a passing verdict on the head while
the LOGIN's newest review names an older commit.
`staleReviewPolicy` IS A POLICY CALL AND IS DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN FOR THE MAINTAINER.
The two obvious scopings are both wrong against this repository's own data, measured
- 'ignore COMMENTED' would make this a no-op. Every review event on #3276, #3288 and
#3227 is COMMENTED -- CodeRabbit's, cursor[bot]'s, greptile's, codex's and the
humans'. Not one APPROVED. It would drop #3276, the example the issue is about.
- 'an author with no review at head is stale' would nag constantly. #3316, #3205 and
#3290 carry ZERO review events, and #3316 and #3205 still carry
`CodeRabbit :: success / Review completed` on their heads. Absence of a review is not
evidence of staleness, and part 3 never reports it. That is a STATED HOLE.
`claimed-verdict` is the NARROWEST rule that still catches #3276: configured author, AND
its context reports success on the head, AND its newest review names a different commit.
Over the 12 open PRs of 2026-08-26 it fires on #3276, #3288, #3227 and #2952 and stays
silent on #3315, #3309 and #2931. `configured-authors` drops the context clause;
`all-authors` drops the identity scope too and flags a human APPROVED across a rebase.
AND IT SHIPS `off`, BECAUSE THE PREMISE IS FALSE FOR THIS REPO'S PRIMARY REVIEWER.
CodeRabbit submits NO REVIEW EVENT AT ALL when a run finds nothing actionable, so
'no review object naming the head' does not mean 'the head was not reviewed'. Measured
live on all four fires:
- #3276 head 1305f778: a real 155 s cycle ON THE HEAD (Review queued 14:09:52 -> in
progress 14:09:55 -> success 14:12:27), and CodeRabbit's walkthrough comment updated
14:12:25Z says 'No actionable comments were generated in the recent review' over
'changes between c26e453d and 1305f778' -- the head, including the commit this rule
called unreviewed. #3288 is identical (181 s cycle, head named). BOTH FALSE.
- #3227 (14 s cycle) and #2952 (9 s) are genuine: their walkthrough comments read
'Reviews paused ... under active development' and CodeRabbit published
'success / Review completed' regardless.
TWO OF FOUR FIRES ARE WRONG, and no structured field separates them: the status is
byte-identical across all four, CodeRabbit publishes no check RUN on any of these heads
so there is no conclusion or output.title to read, and 'a completed review cycle on this
head counts as review' is not a narrowing but a deletion -- clause (b) already requires
success on the head, and a success on the head IS a completed cycle, so it silences the
two real catches too. What is left is cycle DURATION (155/181 s against 14/9 s), an
unversioned timing heuristic on a third party, and the reviewer's PROSE, which the note
above rules out. It also contradicts this file's own stated hole: #3316 has success on
its head and ZERO reviews and is deliberately silent because absence of a review is not
evidence of staleness -- #3276 is the same fact, flipped only by one incidental older
review. So the machinery, the scopings and the four worked examples all ship and the
rule is OFF: it is never adjudicated unless a maintainer opts in, `off` NEVER prints a
tick, and #3227/#2952 stay catchable for anyone who sets it. louistrue's call.
`staleReviewSeverity` applies to a SUPPRESSED finding too. When part 2 has already
quoted the same reviewer the SENTENCE is redundant, so it is said once -- but the
verdict still moves the exit code. Dropping the finding made this knob inoperative and
printed the part 3 tick over a finding the gate had made.
`staleReviewSeverity` is `warn` for the SAME @unwired-by-design reason as
`reviewVerdictSeverity`: whether a bot has re-reviewed the newest push is transient
GitHub state, not a fact about the diff. Like that key it is not defaulted in code.
